Write a dramatic short story with a shocking plot twist based on this prompt:

" So this is how I die... "

So, this is how I die. Alone and afraid. There is a darkness and it grows and grows until it fills your eyes and overflows into the depths of your mind. There is no glimmering light far away. No flash of memories across the back of your eyelids. Only the cold touch of the pavement, leeching the warmth from your cheek. The pain is immense. It is not distant or far away. It is all too real, and it mixes with the fear until your body soils itself unintentionally. The stink of death is foul. You do not think of the ones you left behind, your family or your friends. When the individual is reduced to their base instincts there is room only for yourself. At the end of the line, what it all comes down to is you. You only ever thought about yourself. And you think so much about yourself that eventually you learn to hate yourself, and you lose something important. And when you lose that you lose yourself. And sooner or later the world will lose you. 
 
 
 The worst thing is not the fear. It is not the pain, although it might nearly be that. No. The worst thing was not the sudden finality of that fatal jump. It was not the fear in your veins as you plummeted towards the ground. It is not the pain that reminds you of how you have never been more alive than now, as you lie dying. It was none of these things. The worst thing, the worst thing of all, was that as the air rushed by your arms, and the dreadful certainty of non-existence loomed large over your mind, you felt regret. 
 
 
 And realised that even still, you wanted to live.

Your pregnant wife is rushed to the hospital after an accident. You have to choose between her life or the child's. Only one will survive surgery.

I will never forget the smell. 
 
 It was very late at night when it happened. She had been out with her parents and some asshole ran a red light after a few too many drinks. One moment and everything ended. 
 
 I barely had time to throw on a shirt before I was out the door, breaking every law to get to the hospital. 
 
 They told me that her parents were gone. 
 
 All that was left was two heartbeats holding on desperately for life. 
 
 Only one could survive. 
 
 I remember everything about that moment. The creases in the nurses scrubs and the tears in all their eyes. I remember my knees bruising on the tiled floor and my hands slamming into the wall. I remember screaming my throat raw as I begged them to take me and save them both. 
 
 I remember the smell. The smell of sterility and death. 
 
 It's been hours now. They'll come tell me the news soon. 
 
 There's a crowd waiting, praying, begging. They're here to support me but I don't want it. I just want them both to be here. 
 
 When the doctor comes out he is grim and I know why. 
 
 He takes me to see her. He leaves me alone with her. 
 
 I take her hand and sob, I cry into her shoulder and tell her I'm sorry that I wasn't stronger. That couldn't do it. That I hoped she could forgive me. Please forgive me. 
 
 I don't know how long they left me there with her. It would never be long enough. 
 
 When they handed me a tiny, warm body I was so afraid I would break her. Little green eyes watched me and I could see her in them. She held me finger with a tiny little hand and I cried. 
 
 She would never be gone. Not entirely. 
 
 She would forgive me. I know she would. 
 
 A little hand squeezed my finger tighter as if to comfort me. 
 
 As if to say that I was forgiven. 
 
 And I smiled through the tears.

A Tall Ship

She was called *The Red Paddy*, but only in hushed tones among those that she had bested before and those that had yet to come into contact with her; the words were often harsh, but laced with a begrudging respect and sometimes even admiration for the schooner that seemed to slip out of their grasp as though she was powered by something more than the wind alone. 
 
 She was called that for two reasons: the complexion of her captain and her red cedar construction. She was sleek, svelte, and sat low in the water, with waves often lapping at her bulwark in anything but glass-smooth seas. Rumor was that she was originally commissioned by a lord from the Foreign Office who had spent most of his life as an ambassador to the Ottomans and had it built as a retirement gift to himself and a reminder of his time in the Levant and Anatolia. Word is he planned on racing and traveling with his mistress on it, though that was short-lived once he met her current captain. Displacing just over 170 tons, she was diminutive in size in comparison to even the smallest warship, but she wasn't meant to stand and fight, she was meant to run- and run she did. 
 
 Her current captain was a runner as well- Simon Pearce ran from his creditors, his local constabulary, and even his wife; the only running he didn't do was the actual action itself. Having a ruddy face with jowls like a bulldog and a paunchy midsection, he earned the name Paddy due to his appearance and problems with the drink despite not being Irish by any means. The closest similarity one could draw to him was of an alleycat: opportunistic and kept to himself, but could be quite fierce when backed into a corner. It was through him seizing upon an opportunity of a game of cards with a Lord too drunk to spot a cheat, and fighting off the Lord's retinue that could spot a cheat, that he came into his new vessel. Compared to one another, the captain and his vessel seemed like the antithesis of the other, but they were more similar than what the eye alone took in.
